shadows.name: button-backlit-hover

shadows.name: button-backlit-engaged

motion.name: needle-settle

motion.name: tape-fill

components.name: Instrument Dial
components.description: Level/Plasma readout — circular tick-marked gauge, glowing needle, tabular-mono digital sub-readout, tracked caption below.
components.css: .ds-dial { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; width: 64px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; } .ds-dial-face { position: relative; width: 64px; height: 64px; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 42%, #101512 0%, #0a0d0c 78%); border: 1px solid rgba(120,255,170,0.28); box-shadow: 0 0 10px 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.6) inset, 0 0 6px 0 rgba(57,255,106,0.65); box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-dial-readout { position: absolute; left: 50%; bottom: 11px; transform: translateX(-50%); font-weight: 600; font-size: 11px; color: #e8fff0; text-shadow: 0 0 4px rgba(57,255,106,0.65); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-dial-label { margin-top: 4px; font-size: 9px; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: rgba(57,255,106,0.65); }

components.name: Primary Button (engaged)
components.description: Confirm-forward action (Resume, Restart-on-game-over) — filled phosphor, void-black text, the 'engaged/lit switch' state.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #39ff6a; color: #000000; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 12px 26px; border: 1px solid #39ff6a; clip-path: polygon(8px 0, calc(100% - 8px) 0, 100% 8px, 100% calc(100% - 8px), calc(100% - 8px) 100%, 8px 100%, 0 calc(100% - 8px), 0 8px); box-shadow: 0 0 14px 2px rgba(57,255,106,0.65); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { box-shadow: 0 0 18px 3px rgba(57,255,106,0.65); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #39ff6a; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Danger Button (idle/backlit)
components.description: Destructive action (pause-menu Restart) — dark panel, red hairline border and legend text, backlit-outline idle state.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background: #0a0d0c; color: #ff3b30; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 12px 26px; border: 1px solid #ff3b30; clip-path: polygon(8px 0, calc(100% - 8px) 0, 100% 8px, 100% calc(100% - 8px), calc(100% - 8px) 100%, 8px 100%, 0 calc(100% - 8px), 0 8px); box-shadow: 0 0 6px 0 rgba(255,59,48,0.5); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { box-shadow: 0 0 18px 3px rgba(255,59,48,0.5); } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #39ff6a; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Console Panel Modal
components.description: Shop / pause / tech-tree / game-over container — centered chamfered panel with a title bar and status lamp, over a full-viewport scrim.
components.css: .ds-modal-scrim { position: fixed; inset: 0; background: rgba(2,4,3,0.86); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; } .ds-modal-panel { background: #0a0d0c; border: 1px solid rgba(57,255,106,0.33); clip-path: polygon(20px 0, calc(100% - 20px) 0, 100% 20px, 100% calc(100% - 20px), calc(100% - 20px) 100%, 20px 100%, 0 calc(100% - 20px), 0 20px); box-shadow: 0 0 36px 2px rgba(57,255,106,0.2), 0 4px 24px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.6); padding: 28px 32px; max-width: min(92vw, 420px); } .ds-modal-title-bar { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding-bottom: 10px; margin-bottom: 18px; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(120,255,170,0.14); } .ds-modal-title-bar h2 { margin: 0; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-weight: 600; font-size: 20px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #39ff6a; text-shadow: 0 0 6px #39ff6a55; } .ds-modal-lamp { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: #39ff6a; box-shadow: 0 0 6px 1px #39ff6a; }

components.name: Annunciator Toast
components.description: Wave-caution (amber) and elite-contact (gold) status toasts — chamfered panel, pulsing lamp, tracked-caps message.
components.css: .ds-annunciator { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 9px 20px; background: #0a0d0c; border: 1px solid #ffb000; clip-path: polygon(6px 0, calc(100% - 6px) 0, 100% 6px, 100% calc(100% - 6px), calc(100% - 6px) 100%, 6px 100%, 0 calc(100% - 6px), 0 6px); box-shadow: 0 0 16px 1px #ffb00066; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #ffb000; animation: ds-lamp-flash 1s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-annunciator-lamp { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: #ffb000; box-shadow: 0 0 6px 1px #ffb000; flex-shrink: 0; } @keyframes ds-lamp-flash { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.72; } }

narrative.overview: The HUD reads as an actual cockpit instrument panel, not a themed dashboard. You're not glancing at floating pills — you're cross-checking a glass panel at night with nothing outside the canopy but the void: round tick-marked dial gauges with damped needles, hard-edged chamfered (cut-corner) console panels, backlit-legend switches instead of solid pill buttons, and annunciator lamps that stay dark until something is genuinely wrong. A thin scanline + vignette overlay sits over the whole viewport, like looking through cockpit glass. The color system is literalized as real annunciator-panel convention: phosphor green means normal/go/life, amber means anticipatory caution, red means true danger or a destructive action, and gold marks a target of opportunity (the elite scanner). Nothing lights up amber or red unless it means it — that restraint is the point. The procedural pixel-art ship/enemy/pickup sprites and all gameplay-signal colors are a separate, untouched layer beneath this HUD redesign; this system governs chrome only.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black gunmetal panels with a chamfered (cut-corner) silhouette everywhere a rounded corner used to be — the one exception is the circular instrument dials themselves.
Colored glow is still the system's only depth signal, but it now reads as a backlit legend (an annunciator lamp or an illuminated switch) rather than a decorative halo.
Round tick-marked dial gauges with a damped-needle settle animation for Level and Plasma, backed by a real tabular-mono digital sub-readout.
IBM Plex Mono is used everywhere: numerals, labels, titles, body copy — the project's first deliberate typeface choice.
Modals are centered chamfered console panels with a dark scrim behind them, not full-viewport flush-top sheets — this supersedes the old Flush-Top Modal Rule.

rules.name: The Annunciator Rule
rules.body: A color only appears when its status is true. Amber and red are never decorative — if nothing amber or red is lit, nothing needs your attention.

rules.name: The Real-Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace is only ever attached to a number, a measurement, or a control's own legend — never dropped onto prose to signal 'technical'.

rules.name: The Backlit-Legend Rule
rules.body: A zero-offset colored glow is only earned when it represents a real backlit instrument, never a generic 'lifted card' effect. Where real physical lift is needed (a modal over the scrim), pair the glow with an actual offset shadow.

rules.name: The Chamfer Rule
rules.body: Corners are cut, not curved. A border-radius on a console surface is a regression to the old world; use clip-path chamfering instead. Dial gauges are the sole exception.

dos: Do clip new console surfaces with the chamfer clip-path, not border-radius — the one exception is a genuine circular gauge face.
Do keep amber and red strictly status-true: amber for anticipatory caution, red for real danger or destructive actions, never decorative.
Do route all new HUD text through IBM Plex Mono, and only reach for it because the content is a number, measurement, or control legend.
Do scale both element sizes and fixed position offsets through MOBILE.UI_SCALE_FACTOR — a size-only scale caused a real collision bug in this pass.
Do route new game-entity art through makePixelSprite/drawPixelSprite, and leave gameplay-signal colors (src/constants.js COLORS) alone.
Do give an 'engaged' (filled, void-text) state to any new confirm/unlocked control, distinct from the default backlit-outline idle state.
donts: Don't bring back rounded pills, glassmorphism, or a flush-top full-bleed modal — those belong to the previous world and were deliberately replaced.
Don't add glossy gradients, embossed bevels, or skeuomorphic chrome — a rendered-console (CD-ROM-chrome-style) direction was explicitly considered and rejected for this reason.
Don't use red for anticipatory/warning states — that's Caution Amber's role now; red is reserved for true danger and destructive actions.
Don't introduce a second display typeface as a side effect of an unrelated task — IBM Plex Mono is now the system's one deliberate choice.
Don't add a neutral gray 'lifted card' shadow; every glow must represent a real backlit instrument.
